title: Analytics & Streaming
oneLiner: Ingest, store, and analyze data at scale: Kinesis, Firehose, Glue, Athena, Redshift, and QuickSight.
examWeightNote: Analytics/streaming pipelines appear in High-Performing and decoupling scenarios.
objectives: Differentiate Kinesis Data Streams (real-time, custom consumers) from Firehose (managed delivery to stores).
Build a serverless analytics flow: Firehose → S3 → Glue catalog → Athena → QuickSight.
Choose Athena (ad-hoc SQL on S3) vs Redshift (data warehouse) vs OpenSearch (search/logs).

services.name: Kinesis Data Streams
services.purpose: Real-time, ordered, replayable data streams you build custom consumers on.

services.name: Kinesis Data Firehose
services.purpose: Fully managed delivery of streaming data to S3, Redshift, or OpenSearch (near real-time, no servers).

services.name: AWS Glue
services.purpose: Serverless ETL and a data catalog that makes S3 data queryable.

services.name: Amazon Athena
services.purpose: Serverless, pay-per-query SQL directly over data in S3 — no cluster to manage.

services.name: Amazon Redshift
services.purpose: Managed petabyte-scale data warehouse for complex analytical (OLAP) queries.

services.name: Amazon QuickSight
services.purpose: Serverless BI dashboards and visualizations over your data sources.

keyConcepts: Kinesis Data Streams is for real-time processing with custom consumers and replay (data retained for a window); you manage shards/throughput.
Kinesis Data Firehose is the easy button: fully managed, auto-scaling delivery of streaming data into S3/Redshift/OpenSearch with optional transformation — near real-time, not sub-second.
A classic serverless analytics pipeline: sources → Firehose → S3 (data lake) → Glue (catalog/ETL) → Athena (SQL) → QuickSight (dashboards).
Athena runs ad-hoc SQL on S3 and bills per data scanned — great for occasional queries; Redshift suits heavy, repeated warehouse workloads.
Amazon OpenSearch Service is for full-text search, log analytics, and observability dashboards.
EMR runs managed Spark/Hadoop/Presto clusters for large-scale custom big-data processing.

diagram.caption: A serverless analytics pipeline from streaming ingest to dashboards.
diagram.note: Firehose = managed delivery (near real-time, no code); Data Streams = real-time with custom consumers and replay.

scenarios.scenario: A team wants to land streaming clickstream data into S3 with zero servers to manage and near-real-time delivery, then query it with SQL occasionally.
scenarios.question: Which services fit best?

options.label: Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver to S3, then Athena for ad-hoc SQL
Kinesis Data Streams with a custom app plus a Redshift cluster running 24/7
EMR with a permanent Hadoop cluster

scenarios.explanation: Firehose is the fully managed, no-server path to S3; Athena runs serverless pay-per-query SQL on that S3 data — ideal for occasional analysis without a warehouse.

scenarios.scenario: An application needs sub-second, ordered processing of events by multiple custom consumers, with the ability to replay recent data.
scenarios.question: Which Kinesis option is appropriate?
scenarios.explanation: Data Streams gives real-time, ordered, replayable streams with custom consumers. Firehose is managed delivery to stores and is near-real-time, not sub-second with replay.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between Kinesis Data Streams and Firehose?
options: Streams is for real-time custom processing/replay; Firehose is managed delivery to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch
Firehose is real-time with replay; Streams only delivers to S3
quiz.answer: Streams is for real-time custom processing/replay; Firehose is managed delivery to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch
quiz.explanation: Data Streams = build custom real-time consumers with replay; Firehose = fully managed, near-real-time delivery into stores.

quiz.question: Amazon Athena is best described as:
options: Serverless, pay-per-query SQL over data in S3
quiz.answer: Serverless, pay-per-query SQL over data in S3
quiz.explanation: Athena queries S3 data with standard SQL and bills per data scanned — no infrastructure to manage.

quiz.question: Which service is the managed data warehouse for heavy, repeated analytical (OLAP) queries?
quiz.explanation: Redshift is a columnar, petabyte-scale warehouse optimized for complex analytical queries at scale.

quiz.question: What does AWS Glue provide?
options: Serverless ETL and a data catalog that makes S3 data queryable
quiz.answer: Serverless ETL and a data catalog that makes S3 data queryable
quiz.explanation: Glue crawls/catalogs data and runs serverless ETL jobs, feeding engines like Athena and Redshift Spectrum.

quiz.question: For full-text search and log analytics dashboards, which service fits?
quiz.explanation: OpenSearch Service handles search, log analytics, and observability dashboards.

quiz.question: Amazon QuickSight is used for:
quiz.explanation: QuickSight is AWS's serverless business-intelligence service for dashboards over your data.
